title: Plans and Elevations
seo_title: Year 9 Plans and Elevations Worksheets: Views of 3-D Solids from Above, Front and Side
standard_text: Use the properties of faces, surfaces, edges and vertices of cubes, cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres to solve problems in 3-D; interpret mathematical relationships both algebraically and geometrically.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 plans and elevations worksheets: the plan, front elevation and side elevation of solids made from cubes, numbered plans, and views of cylinders, cones, pyramids and prisms. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plan: from above. Elevation: from the front or side.
key_sub: Each view shows the tallest stack in each column you can see.
body_html:
How it works

A plan is the view of a 3-D solid from directly above. An elevation is the view from the front or the side. Each view is a flat 2-D drawing.

For solids made of cubes: the plan shows one square for each column of cubes. An elevation shows the tallest stack in each column you can see from that direction. Cubes behind other cubes do not show.

Example

Plan of an L-shape made from 4 cubes in a row with 1 cube on top.

From above you see 4 squares.

Answer: 4 squares in a row

Example

Front elevation of the same solid.

The column with 2 cubes is taller.

Answer: 4 squares with 1 on top

Example

A cylinder standing up.

Above: circle. Front: rectangle.

Answer: Circle; rectangle

Common mistakes

  • Swapping the front and side elevations.
  • Drawing a view the wrong way round (mirrored).
  • Showing the heights on a plan drawing. A plan only shows the outline from above.
  • Counting only the cubes you can see when a numbered plan gives the heights.

faq.a: The 2-D view of a solid seen from directly above.

faq.q: What is the difference between a front and a side elevation?
faq.a: The front elevation is the view from the front; the side elevation is the view from the side. They often look different.

faq.q: How do I draw the elevation of a solid made of cubes?
faq.a: For each column you can see, draw the tallest stack. Cubes hidden behind others are not shown.

faq.q: What are the views of a cylinder?
faq.a: The plan is a circle and the front and side elevations are rectangles.

items.q: What is the plan of a solid?
items.e: The plan is the view from directly above.

items.q: What is an elevation?
c: The view from the front or side
items.e: Elevations are views from the front or side.

items.q: A cylinder stands on its circular base. What is its plan?
items.e: From above you see the circular top: a circle.

items.q: A cylinder stands on its circular base. What is its front elevation?
items.e: From the front you see the height and the width: a rectangle.

items.q: A cone stands on its base. What is its front elevation?
items.e: From the side the cone narrows to its point: a triangle.

items.q: A cone stands on its base. What is its plan?
c: A circle with a dot at the centre
items.e: From above you see the circular base and the point above the centre: a circle with a dot at the centre.

items.q: What are the plan and elevations of a sphere?
items.e: A sphere looks the same from every direction: all three are circles.

items.q: A square-based pyramid stands on its base. What is its plan?
c: A square with its diagonals drawn
items.e: From above you see the square base and the edges meeting at the top: a square with its diagonals drawn.

items.q: A square-based pyramid stands on its base. What is its front elevation?
items.e: From the front you see a sloping face: a triangle.

items.q: A solid has plan a circle and front and side elevations that are rectangles. What is it?
items.e: Circle from above and rectangles from the sides: a cylinder.

items.q: A solid has plan a circle and front and side elevations that are triangles. What is it?
items.e: A cone.

items.q: A solid has a plan, front elevation and side elevation that are all squares. What is it?
items.e: A cube.

items.q: A cuboid is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high. What are the dimensions of its plan?
items.e: From above you see the length and the width: 5 cm by 3 cm.

items.q: A cuboid is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high. What are the dimensions of its front elevation (looking at the long side)?
items.e: From the front you see the length and the height: 5 cm by 2 cm.

items.q: A triangular prism lies on one of its rectangular faces. Its end faces the side. What is its side elevation?
items.e: From the end you see the cross-section: a triangle.

items.q: A triangular prism lies on one of its rectangular faces. What is its plan?
items.e: From above you see the sloping rectangular faces: a rectangle (with a line along the top edge).

items.q: Why do two different solids sometimes have the same plan?
c: The plan does not show heights
Every solid has a different plan
items.e: A plan only shows what is seen from above, so the plan does not show heights.

items.q: In an elevation drawn on squared paper, what does a hidden cube behind another one do?
c: It is drawn dashed in red
It does not change the elevation
items.e: A cube hidden behind another is not seen, so it does not change the elevation.

items.q: A solid made of cubes has front elevation 3 squares wide and 2 squares tall. What is the greatest number of cubes in that view?
items.e: 3 × 2 = 6 squares can be seen at most.

items.q: Which view would show the difference between a cylinder and a cuboid with a square base?
c: The side elevation only if it is wider
items.e: From the front both can look like rectangles. The plan shows a circle or a square.
